newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech opposition chief attacks govt draft budget.
newsitem.headline: Czech opposition chief attacks govt draft budget.

text.p: Opposition Czech Social Democratic leader Milos Zeman attacked the government's draft budget and said it should do more on tax evasion and economic crime.
Zeman told parliament the ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) had promised to cut inflation while raising wages and pensions in campaigning for elections earlier this year.

But he noted that the fall in inflation had halted -- the consumer price index rose 8.9 percent year-on-year in September compared with 8.6 percent in the same month last year -- and the promised rise in living standards had not yet materialised.

"I think that the budget can be taken as a promise to citizens. It should not go against promises which were given before the election," he told the debate on the first reading of the 1997 budget, which is balanced.
Zeman said he found the government's spending proposals reasonable, notably on housing, transport and helping exports. He also accepted there was no need to run a budget deficit at present.
But he said the government should present a programme on tackling tax evasion and economic crime.

The opposition plans to seek amendments to the draft budget in the vote, which will possibly be taken later on Wednesday. But the Social Democrat chairman of the parliamentary budget committee, Jozef Wagner, has called on deputies to approve it.
This split in opposition ranks may allow Klaus's minority government to win the vote.
